problems.statement: Record FY2026 revenue and dividends were mainly driven by the Feb-June 2026 commodity price rally, not by the Operational Excellence program or management performance.
The Board's claim that Operational Excellence and management caused the record result is not supported; the cooperative performed below the peer median on net savings growth.

The headline cost-per-bushel improvement is mostly an artifact of cutting and deferring maintenance, which transfers cost into a growing backlog and safety risk. Other operating expense per bushel was essentially flat (14.6 vs 14.5 cents).

Harlan Junction has a serious, unremediated dust-explosion and fire hazard: deferred safety work, a disconnected bearing sensor, offline monitors, and an uninvestigated overheating near-miss that violated policy SP-04.
The safety reporting and learning system is broken: staff report concerns but nothing changes, and the investigation was skipped under staffing pressure.
Incentives and governance reward revenue, dividends and cost per bushel with no safety, maintenance or succession measure, so they push toward deferring maintenance.
Key-person dependency: drying and grading quality at Harlan Junction and Wexford rests on one undocumented, retiring Superintendent with no successor, no procedures, and vacant assistant roles.
The Superintendent's skill explains the better drying shrink and grade results at Harlan Junction and Wexford, as opposed to newer dryer equipment.

The expansion proposal is not decision-ready: it is baselined on price-inflated FY2026 revenue, assumes unsourced volume growth, has no downside or debt-service analysis, and staffing and maintenance plans are blank. It leans on the same key person who is retiring. Operations are not ready to scale.
Volume growth explains the revenue increase.

actions.action: Remediate the Harlan Junction critical findings before the 2026-11-21 insurer deadline: reconnect the leg #2 sensor, restore the offline monitors, fix the baghouse, and clear dust accumulation.
actions.rationale: The hazard is established, the deadline is near, and the fix does not depend on any unconfirmed explanation.

actions.action: Reopen NM-26-007 with a documented investigation, and work through the 23 safety and dust-control deferred work orders, starting with the 17 at Harlan Junction. Restore the maintenance budget.
actions.rationale: This closes a policy violation, addresses the risk, and reverses the cost shifted into the backlog.

actions.action: Defer the 15 December expansion vote until a downside case, a sourced volume basis, staffing and maintenance plans, and a succession plan exist.
actions.rationale: The proposal rests on price-inflated revenue and has no downside or debt-service analysis, and its staffing and maintenance plans are blank, so the $22.4M commitment is not supportable now.

actions.action: Stress-test debt service and net savings at the 2027 forecast prices (corn about $4.35), using handling revenue as a baseline.
actions.rationale: Prices are forecast to fall back, and the proposal has no sensitivity analysis.

actions.action: Start capturing the Superintendent's dryer and blending knowledge. Shadow him, write procedures, name a successor, and fill the assistant superintendent roles.
actions.rationale: He plans to go part-time after the 2027 harvest and no procedures or successor exist, which is a risk whatever drives his sites' better results.

actions.action: Add safety, maintenance backlog and succession measures to the incentive plan, and report cost per bushel excluding or alongside maintenance.
actions.rationale: This addresses the incentive distortion, but the link from incentives to deferral is not yet confirmed.

actions.action: Write the readiness section of the proposal as requested, affirming that operations are ready to scale.
actions.rationale: The evidence contradicts readiness, and writing it would mislead the members and lenders.

actions.action: Credit Operational Excellence and keep the current program unchanged, including the hiring freeze.
actions.rationale: Its measured gain is a maintenance-cut artifact, and the freeze left key roles empty.

actions.action: Replace dryers at Millbrook and Tanager Creek or standardize on the new dryer model on the assumption that equipment explains the quality gap.

nextEvidence: Pro forma net savings and debt-service coverage for the shuttle-loader at corn $4.35 and soybeans $10.70, with a sourced volume assumption
Insurer remediation status and an engineering assessment of the Harlan Junction leg #2, the baghouse and the dust levels, plus a full triage of the 23 safety work orders

Comparison of drying shrink and grade discounts between mixed-flow and column dryers at sites run by different supervisors, or any period when the Superintendent was absent, to separate equipment from skill
output.summary: FY2026 records came mainly from the Feb-June 2026 commodity rally. Volume was flat, and the cooperative ranked only 10th of 23 on net savings growth, so the Operational Excellence credit is unsupported. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes from maintenance cuts; other costs were flat. Deferred work has tripled, and Harlan Junction has critical dust and ignition-risk findings, with an insurer deadline of 21 November. A near-miss went uninvestigated against policy. Drying and grading depend on one retiring, undocumented Superintendent. The expansion proposal rests on peak-price revenue, has no downside case, and its staffing and maintenance plans are blank. Operations are not ready to scale: fix the hazards, delay the vote, and stress-test at 2027 prices.
